instructions: The night before, or at least 2 hours ahead: cut the 2 lb beef into 1-inch chunks and put them in a bowl or a zip-top bag. Add 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp hoisin, 1 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp of the five-spice. Mix with your hands until every piece is coated, then cover it and put it in the fridge.

When you're ready to cook, quarter the onion and slice the ginger into thin coins. Peel and slice the 4 garlic cloves. Trim the 2 lemongrass stalks, cut each one into 3 pieces and bash them with the back of a knife until they split open.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high. Add half the beef in a single layer and leave it alone for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is browned. Turn the pieces and brown another side for 2 minutes, then lift them onto a plate. Stand back a little. It will spatter.
Brown the second half of the beef the same way and add it to the plate.
Turn the heat down to medium and add the last 1 tbsp oil. Add the onion, ginger and lemongrass and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until the onion edges soften and it all smells fragrant.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in the 1 tsp paprika and the remaining 2 tsp five-spice and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste and 1 tbsp dark soy sauce and cook for 1 minute, until the paste turns a shade darker and starts to stick.

Put the beef back in with any juice on the plate. Add the 3 star anise, the 2 bay leaves, the can of broth, 3/4 cup coconut water and 3 cups water. Scrape the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon to lift the browned bits. The beef should be just covered.
Bring it to a boil over high, then skim off any gray foam with a spoon. Turn the heat down to low so it bubbles gently, partly cover the pot and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile, peel the 1 lb carrots and cut them into 1-inch chunks.
Seed and slice the jalapeño into a small bowl. Cut the lime into wedges and pick the Thai basil leaves onto a plate. Put the 1/2 tsp pepper in a little dish with a pinch of salt.

Add the carrots to the pot and simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the carrots and a piece of beef breaks apart when you press it with a spoon. If the beef is still firm, give it another 15 minutes.
Fish out the lemongrass, onion pieces, star anise and bay leaves. Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle it into bowls. Serve with the baguette rolls, the Thai basil, the sliced jalapeño, and the lime wedges with the salt and pepper on the side.
advance_prep_notes: Marinate the beef the night before, or at least 2 hours ahead.
method_notes: All three versions braise beef with lemongrass, star anise and a tomato or annatto red base until tender, add carrots near the end, and serve it with baguette or noodles and fresh herbs. Hungry Huy marinates shank for at least 2 hours in soy, hoisin and bo kho spice, then simmers it in chicken broth, coconut soda and water with tomato paste and dark soy, without searing. Cooking Therapy and Delightful Plate both brown the marinated beef first, and Delightful Plate thickens the stew lightly with cornstarch. This one follows Hungry Huy's marinade and braise, swaps the spice packet for five-spice, uses chuck in place of shank so the parboil step drops out, and browns the beef as the other two do.
